prompt: Spot the first non-repeated string. Complete the firstUnique method so it returns the first element that occurs exactly once in the array, or null when there is no such element.
explanation: This is a two-pass problem: the first pass builds a Map from each string to how many times it appears (getOrDefault makes the counting a one-liner), and the second pass walks the ORIGINAL array in order, returning the first string whose count is 1. Iterating the array again, rather than the map, is what guarantees the answer is the first unique element by position.
hints: You cannot know a string is unique until you have seen the whole array, so plan on two passes.
Pass 1: build a Map<String, Integer> of counts using counts.getOrDefault(item, 0) + 1.
Pass 2: loop over the array (not the map) and return the first item whose count equals 1; return null after the loop.
